defects.defect: The daily Google sign-in check is taken out of wave A and made the first build step of wave B. Tony approved S14, whose words are 'One daily check is added with mail', the wave A he saw held it, and the card exists so that an expired sign-in does not first show up as a missing or empty morning text. Both 07:00 texts would run from the end of wave A into wave B with only the scheduler's failed-job alert behind them. The proposal says this itself and gives size as the only reason.

Wave I holds the screen-control pilot alone, and its own note says it 'ends with an answer about one chore, not with a daily feature'. If step zero fails, the plan leaves nothing behind, so it does not end in a state a parent would notice. Waves H and I are 14.25 hours each, under the 15-hour floor the proposal sets itself, and they spend two exit gates and two sign-offs where the other two proposals use one wave of about 20 hours (phone first, screen control last, each in its own phases).

The second piece named to give way in wave A is 'did I get an email about X?'. The fact sheet records the lookup as built in wave A, and the brief lets only the second inbox flex ('both parents' inboxes as far as they fit'). After the paper pair, Jordan's inbox should give way before the lookup.

Waves A, B and C are each within an hour of the ceiling (25.0, 24.5 and 24.25 hours by my count). After one overrun in A the paper pair moves into B and the day out leaves A to C for wave D, so the A to C that Tony would get is not quite the A to C drawn.

Voice memos need only photos and PDFs (wave B) and add no way out, yet they wait for the eighth plan, behind the browser, the group chat, printing and lights. That breaks the proposal's own rule (the earliest wave with room; wave G has about 7 hours free) and puts a feature both parents could use near the end.
Wave C's get-ready does not record the default Tony was told and left unchanged: no chat excerpts kept overnight. The other two proposals record it.

Get ready records the shared handbook folder and shared database rows as 'Tony's choices of 12 Oct' to step outside 'one data domain per person'. He chose the features. The fact sheet records that he was told what the group chat and the dose log change, and nothing of the kind for the handbook or the database. It should read as a departure from his own roadmap decision that he signs in this wave; the sign-off page already carries the line.

Wave A is stated as 25 hours and 49 steps only because getting ready is counted at 0.75 hours and 3 steps. The earlier definition Tony saw, after two audits, counted 1.25 hours and 4 steps. At that rate wave A is 25.5 hours and 51 steps, and the proposal adds that Jordan's lookup checks may be another half hour. So the design as drawn (both inboxes in A) is not what is likely to happen: Jordan's inbox, about which Tony answered 'Yes. She's agreed', opens wave B. The definition should say that plainly instead of drawing A at exactly the limit. The same half hour is missing from every wave's figure.

Wave A then ends with both 07:00 texts running, no printed line on what a scheduled text is and how Tony switches it off, and nothing for Jordan on how to tell that Happy is down. Nothing Tony said moves them; the reason is size.

The day out leaves A to C for wave D. Tony saw it in wave C, and the earlier definition's own rule lets it sit at the end of wave B when nothing is carried in. Wave B has the room (22.25 hours by my count) unless Jordan's inbox arrives from wave A.

The first wave after C is mostly for Tony alone: the weekly text, the page watch and the project check-ins are his only, and the conflict watch reaches Jordan only if her copy is switched on. Jordan notices the day out and little else, while the pages and logs both parents use wait one more plan. The notes say D and E can swap but do not say why this order is the default.

graft.what: Wave A's size said as it is and one fixed decision point. With both inboxes, the lookup and the sign-in check, wave A is about 25.5 hours and 51 steps at the earlier definition's 1.25-hour get-ready. Take use's rule: when Tony's own 07:00 text and the sign-in check are live, if the plan is over its hours, the lookup is built for Tony and Jordan's inbox opens wave B; the sign-in check never gives way. Keep use's line that until then Tony's school lines cover the school mail, which both parents receive. Risk's wave B has the room: about 24.0 hours with her inbox.

The paper pair done in wave A's eight-day wait. Keep the stop-and-check sheet and Jordan's half page counted in wave B, as risk has them, but allow T8 and the two pages to be done while wave A waits for day 8 of the Google sign-in, as deps's phase 'fills the eight-day wait' does and use's notes allow. Wave A then still ends as Tony saw it whenever the first week runs to plan.

The day out (F028) as the last build phase of wave B, where deps and use both place it, so it stays inside A to C as Tony saw it. It becomes wave B's first give-way, to the front of wave D, when Jordan's inbox is carried in from wave A. Wave B is about 24.0 hours either way (with the day out, or with Jordan's inbox in its place). Wave D is about 14.75 hours when the day out stays in B: a light plan that keeps its room for what gives way from B and C.

Wave C opening with the 'try it first' phase the earlier wave C had: T5 and T7 on eval-only and throwaway agents before any rule is written (use's phase 2; deps does the same just before its plugin phase). This puts T7 ahead of T5's scheduling-tool turn, as the reminders card asks, and keeps the rest of risk's order.

The America/New_York zone named on the 21:00 job. Tony wrote '9pm EST'; the config's zone keeps the text at 21:00 local time through the clock change, and deps is the only proposal that writes the zone on the job.

Two ways of carrying 'Tony provides X at execution'. First, the get-ready line in the shared pages and logs wave that asks early for what takes a parent time to gather (the school district's calendar, the facts for the family pages, a short label for each child). Second, the tony_provides entries for the decisions a failed test hands him (the day-8 search, T4, T5, T7), so each is listed in the wave that needs it.

One line in the last wave's get-ready, taken from the app card: the iPhone app is a first paired device and not the connected idle iPhone Tony once described, so his own example of an advanced ability is not read as delivered.

The note that wave C's house-rules plugin go-live check includes both 07:00 mail texts still arriving, written into the plugin phase's goes-live line (risk checks a text, a weather question and a mail lookup, not the scheduled texts).

notes: Size basis (estimates, not measurements): each wave is its cards' hours from sizes.json plus 1.25 hours to get ready and a 3-hour exit gate, the audited figures of the earlier definition, at two steps an hour (the earlier wave A was 24.5 hours and 49 steps). fits_one_plan is true at or under 25 hours and 50 steps. An estimate cannot tell 25.0 from 25.5 hours, so a false on wave A means 'at the ceiling, expect its named piece to move', not 'cannot be built'.

No blocker in any proposal. All three place all 36 planned cards exactly once and leave out only the two parked cards (F072, AUT-06). None breaks a dependency listed in sizes.json. Mail reading is wave A in all three, with both inboxes and 'did I get an email about X?'.

None makes a wave or a card wait on an unanswered question or a missing detail. What is conditional is a test result (T1, T4, T5, T6, T7, T9, the browser image build, step zero) with the fallback its card names, and each missing detail is under tony_provides.
None contains the children's first names, the school district's name, the home town, a phone number, an email address or a key.

None brings back what an approved simplification dropped (the notification-policy plugin, texts into the other parent's chat, the renewals table, the outage notice). The cards I spot-checked against the fact sheet (the weekly text, the page watch, lights and speakers, the iPhone app) are in their simplified form in all three.

All three carry Tony's answers of 12 Oct as given: one firewall rule before mail, the outbound proxy before web reading, the tripwire waiting for local models, photos and PDFs on the cloud model, reminders for Tony only, the shared Google calendar, one evening text at 21:00 Eastern, Jordan's own Gmail sign-in, and the confirm step before the dose log.

Why risk is the base: where the three differ it follows Tony's approved wording most closely. The sign-in check is added with mail (S14), his unchanged defaults are written into the waves that touch them, and every wave from B on keeps room for the piece that gives way before it, which is what keeps 'each wave is one plan' true after the first overrun. Its order after C comes from the roadmap's rule of one new kind of risk at a time, not from a guess about what the family uses. Its faults are an understated wave A and two moves (the paper pair, the day out) further from what Tony saw than they need to be; the grafts address those.

Not grafted: use's order after C (shared pages and logs before the watchers). It ends the fourth plan in something both parents notice, but it rests on a guess about use that Tony has not made. Risk's notes already say D and E can swap at his word; the merged definition should keep that line and say the default order is by risk.
